column2: Completion of both houses after twenty years, assembly of all elders in Zion and bringing the covenant ark from David's city identified as Zion remain.
Athanin alone supplies the month in this short continuation; a seventh-month festival explanation is not imported.
Priests carry the ark, beginning the equipment sentence that continues into verse 4; Levites are not added.
The tent of testimony and all its holy utensils complete the preceding carrying clause, retaining the repeated tent designation.
King and all Israel stand before the ark sacrificing uncountable sheep and cattle; no numerical total replaces uncountable here.
The ark's place is the inner sanctuary, Holy of Holies, beneath the cherubim's wings, with every successive location retained.
For explains the wings spread over the ark's place and covering the ark and its holy things from above.
column3: Holy things is retained rather than silently identifying the objects as carrying poles.

column2: Projected consecrated things, visible ends from the holy places before the sanctuary and invisibility outside preserve the selected vocabulary and contrast.
column3: The consecrated objects and exact sightline remain unresolved; neither poles nor an until-this-day clause is imported.

column2: Only two stone covenant tablets are inside, placed by Moses at Horeb, with the exodus covenant explanation retained.
The priests' departure from the Holy Place and cloud filling the house retain the temporal relation and setting.
The priests' inability to stand and minister is caused by the cloud and explained by the house filled with divine glory.
The repeated king, turning face, blessing all Israel and standing assembly remain after the selected gap at verses 12–13.
Blessing this day names the Lord's mouth speaking concerning David and hands fulfilling, retaining the bodily imagery and third-person reference.
The quotation includes no city previously chosen in any Israelite tribe, followed by explicit Jerusalem choice and David choice.
column3: Tribe interprets the scepter term contextually; Jerusalem is not omitted to match a shorter parallel.

column2: Building for the name of the Lord God of Israel is in David's heart, preserving intention before the restriction.
The Lord commends the heart's intention in ordinary address to David, with the repeated came-into-your-heart clause retained.
The restriction on David and promise to the son coming from his sides preserve the selected bodily expression rather than substituting loins.
Divine establishment and Solomon's rising, sitting and building retain their sequence and the repeated fulfillment relation.
The ark's place, covenant within it, the Lord's covenant with the fathers and His bringing them out remain without reducing the covenant to an unexpressed document label.
Solomon stands before altar and whole assembly with hands spread heavenward, preparing the direct divine address.
No God like Thee, heaven above/earth below, covenant and mercy and the singular servant walking wholeheartedly remain.
The relative continuation identifies David, and direct Thou/Thy preserves mouth-speaking and hand-fulfillment this day.
Prayer to God encloses His promise to David: the outer Thy/Thou and inner human yours/your/you remain correctly distinguished, including the conditional children's obedience.
The Lord God of Israel is addressed again and confirmation of His word to David requested; the emphatic indeed remains.
The question retains dwelling with people on earth, heaven and heaven of heaven insufficient, and the house built for God's name.
column3: But and how much less express the rhetorical transition and comparison idiom; the initial hoti and plēn construction remain open to closer syntactic review.

column2: Supplication, rejoicing, before Thee, to Thee and this day remain in the petition rather than replacing terpsis with a generic cry.
column3: The unusual rejoicing term and future-form petition interpreted as Look remain provisional.

column2: Both day-and-night expressions, eyes toward the house, the quoted name promise and hearing prayer toward this place remain.
Servant and Israel's supplication, prayer toward this place, heavenly dwelling, acting and mercy retain the full petition sequence.
column3: Future forms are expressed as requests in the prayer context, not a new independent prediction.

column2: Sin against a neighbor, an oath-curse taken upon oneself and declaration before the altar retain the selected legal scene.
column3: The oath's subject and exagoreuo as declaration versus confession remain provisional; this does not impose a particular judicial procedure.

column2: Hearing, acting and judging Israel lead to condemnation of lawless conduct upon its owner's head and vindication according to righteousness.
Defeat before enemies, sin against God, return, acknowledgment, prayer and pleading retain the conditional sequence.
column3: Have sinned gives idiomatic anteriority within the English when-clause; the Greek future sin and subsequent futures are not claimed to have past morphology.

column2: The response asks heavenly hearing, mercy for Israel's sins and return to the fathers' given land, retaining all three actions.
Closed heaven and no rain, sin, prayer, acknowledgment, turning from sins and God's humbling remain.
column3: The future sin clause is rendered idiomatically as prior cause in the English condition; exact temporal force remains provisional.

column2: Mercy concerns both singular servant and Israel; the explanation that Thou wilt show the good way and the request for rain on inherited land remain.
Famine, death, scorching, locust, mildew, an enemy in one city, every calamity and pain are all retained in the petition's extended condition.
column3: The inherited if-series smooths the unusual hoti estai before scorching; its causal or explanatory force and scope over the following conditions remain unresolved.

column2: Every prayer and supplication, any person, each heart's affliction and spread hands toward the house retain universal and individual scope.
column3: Affliction interprets the touch/plague term contextually; no diagnosis of an inward disease is asserted.

column2: Hearing from the prepared heavenly dwelling, mercy, action and recompense according to ways depend on God's unique knowledge of every human heart.
Fear of God throughout life on the land given to our fathers preserves the switch from their to our within the prayer.
The foreigner not belonging to Thy people remains the short selected clause; distant-land and reputation explanations are not imported.
The selected plural they come and pray remains after singular foreigner, preserving the number shift.
column3: When is an interpretive English link for the coordinated future clause within the petition; the plural is not silently regularized to he.

column2: Heavenly hearing and doing the foreigner's requests aim at all peoples knowing and fearing God's name and recognizing the named house.
War against enemies, the way God turns them, prayer in the Lord's name and orientation toward chosen city and house remain.
column3: When interprets the introductory hoti in the recurring petition structure; turning is not silently replaced with sending.

column2: Hearing both supplication and prayer from heaven and doing justice for them remain as uphold their cause.
column3: The written eisakousei form occurs within second-person address; the petition rendering follows that context without claiming an apparatus decision on spelling or person.

column2: Future universal sin, divine action against them, surrender to enemies and captivity in land far and near retain all stages.
column3: Trouble supplies the unexpressed object of bring upon; far and near retains and rather than changing the conjunction to or.

column2: Heart-turning in the deportation land, return, pleading and the three confessions sinned, acted lawlessly and done wrong remain.
Whole heart and soul, enemy land where God deported them, prayer toward land, chosen city and named house retain direct divine agency and the three directions.
Hearing from the prepared heavenly dwelling remains a short continuation leading into mercy in verse 50; an extra justice clause is not inserted.
Wrongs, sins and faithless acts are distinguished, and divine granting of compassion precedes captors' compassion.
column3: So that gives the final coordinated compassion clause a result relation in English; it does not negate the selected future assertion.

column2: For grounds the request in people and inheritance, brought from Egypt's iron-smelting furnace; the furnace metaphor remains.
Both eyes and ears open toward the servant's and people's supplications retain the fuller selected sensory wording and all their calls.
God's setting apart from every people, Moses' mediated word and the exodus close with the repeated Lord, Lord.

The complete poem and attached continuation were read together: made-known sun, dwelling in gloom, command to build My house for yourself, dwelling in newness and Book of Song question all remain. Proposed lines separate introduction and sun clause, then the continuation's poetic clauses and citation question.
column3: Speaker boundaries, command rather than completed building, My/yourself relationship, newness and the feminine this reference remain unresolved. Ordinary yourself follows the provisional divine-command reading. The negative-presentative question is rendered idiomatically Is this not written; the record does not equate Book of Song with a differently named source.

column2: Finishing all prayer and supplication, rising from the altar, having knelt and hands spread toward heaven preserve the posture sequence without suppressing earlier standing.
Standing and loud blessing address the whole Israelite assembly, opening the third-person divine benediction.
This-day blessing, promised rest, not one failed good word and mediation through Moses retain every scope marker.
The wish for divine presence as with the fathers and both negatives, not abandoning and not turning us away, remain.
Inclining hearts toward Himself leads to all ways and all commandments and ordinances given the fathers, preserving the repeated all.
The speech moves from third-person Lord our God to direct Thy servant and Thy people; day/night and each day's matter retain both temporal expressions.
All peoples' knowledge, the emphatic He is God and no other preserve the exclusive confession without adding another predicate.
Our hearts, completeness toward our God, devout walking and command-keeping this day remain; your hearts is not substituted.
King and all sons of Israel sacrifice before the Lord, retaining the opening communal action.
Twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep are peace offerings; king and all Israel's sons dedicate the house.
Consecration of the court center, burnt offering, sacrifices and peace-offering fat are explained by the bronze altar's insufficient size.
The great assembly extends from Hamath's entrance to Egypt's River; house, repeated Lord our God and eating/drinking/rejoicing for seven days remain.
column3: Seven is not expanded to fourteen from a parallel; the singular participles' collective scope is rendered with the king and assembly context.

column2: On day eight he dismisses and blesses the people, who go each to his tent with joy for goodness to David and Israel.
column3: The singular blessing agent is retained; the people are not made the agents blessing the king.
